# openstatus_tcp_monitor (Resource)

Manages an OpenStatus TCP monitor that periodically checks the availability of a TCP endpoint.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "openstatus_tcp_monitor" "db" {
  name        = "Database Port Check"
  uri         = "db.example.com:5432"
  periodicity = "1m"
  timeout     = 10000
  active      = true
  regions     = ["fly-iad", "fly-fra"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the monitor.
- `uri` (String) Host and port to monitor (e.g., `db.example.com:5432`).
- `periodicity` (String) Check frequency. Valid values: `30s`, `1m`, `5m`, `10m`, `30m`, `1h`.

### Optional

- `timeout` (Number) Connection timeout in milliseconds (0–120000). Default: `45000`.
- `degraded_at` (Number) Latency threshold in milliseconds after which the monitor is considered degraded.
- `retry` (Number) Number of retries before marking the monitor as down (0–10). Default: `3`.
- `active` (Boolean) Whether monitoring is active. Default: `false`.
- `public` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is publicly visible. Default: `false`.
- `description` (String) Description of the monitor.
- `regions` (List of String) Monitoring regions. Valid values: `fly-iad`, `fly-ams`, `fly-hkg`, `fly-jnb`, `fly-syd`, `fly-gru`, `koyeb-was`, `koyeb-fra`, `koyeb-sgp`, `railway-us-west1`, `railway-us-east1`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the monitor.
- `status` (String) Current status of the monitor.

## Import

Import using the monitor ID:

```shell
terraform import openstatus_tcp_monitor.example <monitor_id>
```
